sentences.text:

 -versus-
 Arati Sahoo & Anr. .... Opp. Party
 Coram:
 Justice Chittaranjan Dash
 Order
Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner.

2. By means of this application the Petitioner seeks indulgence of this Court to quash the order dated 17.12.2022 passed by the learned Judge, Family Court, Baripada in Criminal Proceeding No.
105 of 2022.
3. The Present Petitioner and Opp. Party No-1 solemnized their marriage at Akhandalamani Mandir under Puri P.S. on 08.02.2013 as per caste, custom and rites and the said marriage is still subsisting.
One male child was born out of the wedlock between the parties on dated 19.12.2013 namely Ayushman arrayed as Opp. Party No-2 in the case.
The parties lived a happy married life till the year 2014.
The dissension arose between the parties in the year 2015.

Opp. Party No-1 subsequently lodged an FIR against the Petitioner and in-laws registered vide Baripada Town P.S. No. // 2 //
27/22 and the case is pending before the SDJM, Baripada U/S 498A/506/34 IPC and Section 4 of the DP Act.
Besides that, the Petitioner filed guardian Misc. Case U/S. 25 of Guardians and Wards Act vide CP No- 91 of 2016 which is currently pending before the learned Judge, Family Court, Puri.

4. The Petitioner herein challenges the order dated 17.12.2022 whereby he is directed to pay Rs.8,000/- per month towards interim maintenance to the opposite parties from the date of the order apart from a payment of Rs.5,000/- towards litigation expenses.
The opposite parties claimed Rs.15,000/- per month towards maintenance alleging cruelty and ill treatment by the petitioners- Bibaswan Sahoo vs Arati Sahoo & Anr. ....

sentences.text:
Opp. Party on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96714195/
1 husband forcing them to live separately.
It was, inter alia, claimed that they have no source of income and this petitioner gets Rs.30,000/- per month from his service apart from annual income of Rs.1,00,000/- from other sources.
The petitioner-husband filed his objection urging that the wife left his company without reasonable cause and that he has an income of Rs.10,000/- per month.
The husband filed Memo to treat his objection filed in the main application as the objection to interim petition.

5. The learned Judge, Family Court by order dated 17.12.2022 directed the Petitioner to pay Rs.5,000/- per month to the wife and Rs.3,000/- per month to the son towards interim maintenance from the month of December, 2022 and payable within the first week of each succeeding month and a sum of Rs.5000/- towards one time litigation expenses.

Without going into the merits of the case, this Court on the consent of the learned counsel for the Petitioner directs the Petitioner to pay a sum of Rs.3000/- (Rupees Three Thousand only) instead of Rs. 5000/- to the Petitioner No.1 wife besides Rs. 3000/- in respect to the OP-2-son as directed by the learned court below towards interim maintenance.
The petitioner is directed to deposit the arrear maintenance, if any by the 10th of next month of besides current maintenance.
The other directions issued by the learned court below remain unaltered.
It is also directed that the Petitioner to pursue his case before the learned court below since the interim order will merge with the final order no sooner the final application is disposed of.

Needless to say that while considering the main application, the learned Judge, Family Court shall keep in mind the principles enunciated by the Apex Court in the matter of Rajnesh Vs. Neha reported in (2021) 2 SCC 324.

sentences.text: The CRLMP is disposed of accordingly.
